# `formula-detect` fixtures

Committed fixtures for the page-level formula detector
(`src/formula/detect.rs`, model `pix2text-mfd-1.5`, an Ultralytics YOLO11m detect export).

Everything here is generated by the **independent** Python reference
[`tools/formula_detect_reference.py`](../../../../tools/formula_detect_reference.py), which
uses only `numpy` + `onnxruntime` + `Pillow` (never the `ultralytics` package) and
re-implements letterbox -> head output -> `scale_boxes` -> class-aware NMS itself:

```powershell
$env:RAPID_OCR_MODEL_ROOT='<workspace>\OCR-Model'
python tools/formula_detect_reference.py
```

## Files

| file | content |
| --- | --- |
| `page.png` | white 768x384 RGB canvas, `formula-golden/formula_text.png` pasted at 1.7x at `(40, 48)` |
| `golden.json` | geometry + raw head boxes + final polygons for `page.png` |
| `page_scaled.png` | white 1152x576 RGB canvas, `formula_text.png` pasted at 2.55x at `(40, 84)` |
| `golden_scaled.json` | same for `page_scaled.png` (letterbox scale 2/3, i.e. non-unit scale-back) |

`golden*.json` keys:

- `image`, `image_size`, `pasted_rect`, `paste_scale`, `source_image`: synthetic-page ground truth;
- `input_size`, `confidence_threshold`, `iou_threshold`, `max_detections`, `class_names`: settings;
- `letterbox`: `{scale, left, top, new_size}` — the reference's letterbox geometry, compared
  field-by-field against the Rust implementation;
- `raw_boxes`: every anchor above the confidence threshold, **in letterboxed input pixels**
  (before `scale_boxes` and before NMS) — this is what lets the Rust tests drive its pure
  `scale_back` + `nms` functions without an ONNX session;
- `boxes`: the final polygons in original image pixels, with class id/name and score.

## Measured reference results

| fixture | letterbox | raw > conf | after NMS | detection | IoU with `pasted_rect` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page.png` | scale 1.0, left 0, top 192 | 10 | 1 | `isolated` 0.680487, `(115.76, 62.42)-(715.61, 280.85)` | 0.6746 |
| `page_scaled.png` | scale 2/3, left 0, top 192 | 10 | 1 | `isolated` 0.773576, `(144.64, 104.93)-(1052.08, 434.43)` | 0.6843 |

Rust reproduces the reference polygons to `0e0` (`page.png`) and `3.1e-5` px
(`page_scaled.png`) after scale-back + NMS; the model-backed Rust test reproduces the full
detection to `0.0` px / `0.031` px respectively.

## Why the formula is pasted scaled up

`pix2text-mfd-1.5` is very sensitive to the absolute size of the formula inside the
768x768 network input. Pasting `formula_text.png` at its native 420x160 onto a 768x384
page leaves it at the same size in the input and the `isolated` head stays at ~`0.0015`
(max over all 12096 anchors) — i.e. **no detection at all** at the default 0.25 threshold.
The same page with the formula pasted at 1.7x reaches ~`0.71`. The fixture therefore uses
a known, recorded 1.7x (and 2.55x) paste so that the "detector must find the formula we
pasted" assertion is meaningful; the pasted rectangle is still exact ground truth.

The native-size case is not lost: `src/formula/detect.rs` keeps it covered by the pure
`decode_output`/`scale_back`/`nms` unit tests, which do not depend on model confidence.
